description.value:
This pursuit opens discoveries reflecting your research into vanished civilizations. Each time you gain a new discovery, you may take one from the list below instead, given alphabetically.

Archive Research. Your fieldwork has uncovered a wealth of Force lore: you learn three at-will force powers of your choice, on top of your normal number of powers known.

Force Combat Knowledge. Studying Jedi and Sith fighting techniques earns you proficiency in simple lightweapons, plus knowledge of one lightsaber form of your choice.

It Belongs in a Museum (9th level required). Your unmatched knowledge of antiquities lets you treat any d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10 on Intelligence (Lore) checks or ability checks made with your archaeologist's kit.

Localized Survey (13th level required). Rather than examining a single object, you can spend a use of Psychometric Analysis to instead attune to your surroundings, investigating a space up to 50 feet on a side for at least 1 minute. Each minute spent grants a vision of recent events there, reaching back a number of days equal to your scholar level, revealing one significant event at a time starting with the most recent.

You can sustain this investigation for a number of minutes equal to your scholar level, requiring concentration throughout as though concentrating on a power. You must finish a short or long rest before using this feature again.

Making This Up As You Go (17th level required). You can now cast a power overpowered to 4th level twice before needing a rest, rather than once.

Telekinetic Ministrations (9th level required). Once between long rests, you can cast telekinesis at 5th level without spending any force points.

The Years and the Mileage. While you are your own Critical Analysis target, you may substitute your universal forcecasting ability for Wisdom on Insight or Survival checks.

Tomb of the Ancients (5th level required). As a reaction to taking damage, you can wrap yourself in the Force until the end of your next turn, gaining resistance to the triggering damage type, temporary hit points equal to 1d10 plus your universal forcecasting ability modifier plus your scholar level (which may absorb the blow entirely), and a speed reduced to 0 for the duration. You must complete a short or long rest before using this feature again.
